title: [SeatMap][Response] Verify GetSeatMap now sets getSeatMapOfferId and getSeatMapResponceID collection variables and that Book consumes them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId when SeatMap precedes it.
request_summary: Book (Galileo/EGY, SV386 CAI-JED 2026-11-19, 1 ADT, no seat) with ResponseId/selectedOfferId taken straight from the GetSeatMap response
response_summary: 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 after 32.6 s - host error 12008 "INVALID CREDIT CARD DETAILS ... failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state with gdsPnr HNC0JP"; no pnr/bookingToken returned
expected: GetSeatMap returns 200 with non-empty offerId/responseId; Book accepts them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId and returns pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR without AddPassenger's IDs being re-sent
actual: Half confirmed, half blocked. GetSeatMap returned non-empty offerId/responseId (both re-issued: different from AddPassenger's), and Book accepted them as its ResponseId/selectedOfferId (no ID or validation error; it ran the full supplier round-trip). It then failed at Galileo's ticketing step, so no pnr/bookingToken/gdsPNR came back. Book cannot complete for Galileo/EGY on this host. All 10 Book calls that passed request validation ended with the same HTTP 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (host error 12008: "INVALID CREDIT CARD DETAILS the reservation failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state with gdsPnr ..."), after 31-51 s, and returned no pnr/bookingToken; all 3 BookAfterHold calls fail the same way (409, "Indicates FOP application failed: CHECK DATE"). This looks like an expired or invalid form-of-payment card on the EGY Galileo credentials (an environment problem, not an API defect), so no booking can be created or read back. The Postman collection-variable assignment is script-side and not observable over raw HTTP.
evidence: GetSeatMap responseId == AddPassenger responseId: false; offerId equal: false; Book 409 in 32.6 s (gdsPnr HNC0JP); same failure on 9 other Book attempts (31-51 s)

plain.e: Confirm the seat-map step hands a usable reference to the booking step, and that booking accepts it
plain.q: Searched a one-way flight from Cairo to Jeddah (2026-11-19) for one adult, opened the seat map, then booked using the seat map's own reference (no seat chosen)
plain.s: The seat map opened with a valid reference and booking accepted it, but the airline system refused to issue the ticket (invalid credit card on the account); no booking reference came back

title: [SeatMap][Request] Validate a cellID obtained from one offer's GetSeatMap response is rejected when submitted in Book for a different offer.
endpoint_or_flow: Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap (x2 offers) -> Book
request_summary: Book on offer E2 (SV386 CAI-JED 2026-11-22) with seat cellCode 34-F but cellId = the cellID issued for seat 33-H on a different offer E1 (SV386 CAI-JED 2026-11-21); two independent Search -> FareConfirm -> AddPassenger -> GetSeatMap chains
response_summary: 400 NDC-INT-TEC-A0001 in 0.1s: "Seat 'CellCode' value '34-F' does not match the seat identified by 'CellId' ('33-H') for passenger ... on segment ..."; no booking created
expected: Request is rejected with a 4xx validation error (exact shape UNKNOWN per 7.9) because the cellID embeds the originating offer and is bound to the offer it was issued for
actual: Rejected as expected, and BUG-07 did NOT reproduce. Galileo decodes the cellId, finds it names seat 33-H (the other offer's seat), compares it with the submitted cellCode 34-F and refuses the request with a specific 400 in 0.1 s, before any supplier call; no booking and no held reservation were created. This is the first supplier on which the foreign-cellId check works (GulfAir and FlyAdeal accept it and silently drop the seat). Note the check is code-vs-id consistency; whether an id of the SAME seat number from another offer is refused was not separable here (the token is just "<seat>~0B5").
evidence: Book 400 in 0.1s; Context: Seat 'CellCode' value '34-F' does not match the seat identified by 'CellId' ('33-H'); no pnr, no gdsPnr

plain.e: Confirm a seat code taken from one flight offer is refused when used on a different offer
plain.q: Opened seat maps for two separate offers, then booked on the second offer with seat 34-F but using the seat code copied from the first offer's seat 33-H
plain.s: Refused at once with a clear 400 error saying the seat code does not match the seat the token identifies; no booking was created
plain.x: The request should be refused
plain.a: Confirmed — this airline does check the token. The earlier defect (BUG-07), where a foreign token was accepted and the seat silently dropped, did not appear

title: [Book][Request] Validate graceful rollback (no orphaned PNR or charge) when the supplier's seat allocation call fails or times out after Book is submitted with a seat selection.
request_summary: Book with a seat selection (seat 33-E, valid cellCode/cellId, SV386 CAI-JED 2026-11-20) in a scenario where the supplier-side step fails after the request is accepted - here Galileo's ticketing step (invalid credit card on the credentials), which fails reproducibly (10 of 10 Book calls that reach the supplier)
response_summary: 409 NDC-INT-UNC-Z9999 (host error 12008) after 41.8 s; no pnr and no bookingToken in the response; the message itself says the reservation "failed at Ticketing stage and still at the hold state with gdsPnr HNC0JN"
expected: Response is an error; either no pnr is returned, or a Retrieve shows the booking without the failed seat and without a fee - i.e. no orphaned booking or charge is left behind (candidate HTTP 422/502; exact behaviour UNKNOWN)
actual: Executed on a real supplier-side failure (not the seat-allocation failure the case names, but the same property: the supplier rejects a step after Book was accepted). Result: the API returns a generic 409 with no pnr/bookingToken, but the supplier reservation is NOT rolled back - Galileo keeps a live held PNR (HNC0JN) that the caller can neither retrieve (no pnr/bookingToken) nor cancel, and the only handle is a gdsPnr buried in the free-text error message. Every one of the 10 failed Books left such an orphan (HNC0JP, HNC0JN, HNC0JQ, HNC0JV, HNC0JY, HNC0K0, HNC0K1, HNC0K2, HNC0K3, HNC0K4). This violates "no orphaned booking" and is filed as new defect BUG-24 (related to BUG-16/BUG-12, where Book errors hid a created booking). The cause here (invalid card) is environmental; the missing rollback and the missing identifiers in the error are not.
evidence: 10 Book calls -> 10 409 responses, each naming a distinct held gdsPnr (HNC0JP, HNC0JN, HNC0JQ, HNC0JV, HNC0JY, HNC0K0, HNC0K1, HNC0K2, HNC0K3, HNC0K4); none returns pnr or bookingToken; error body fields: Status, TransactionId, ErrorCode, ErrorMessage, Context, OriginalSupplierRequest, OriginalSupplierResponse

plain.e: Confirm a failure at the airline after booking leaves no orphan booking or charge
plain.q: Booked a seat on a Cairo to Jeddah flight; the airline system failed at the ticket-issue step (invalid credit card), which is a real airline-side failure after the booking was accepted
plain.s: The API returned a generic error with no booking reference, but the airline system kept a held reservation that nobody can find or cancel through the API; this happened on every failed booking (10 of 10)
plain.x: An error and a clean rollback (no orphan booking)
plain.a: New defect BUG-24 — failed bookings leave untraceable held reservations behind
